SHARE-002.ralphStory: Discovered during DISC-002 surface extraction; scope described by behavior-surface-rules.json

SHARE-003.ralphStory: Discovered during DISC-002 surface extraction; scope described by behavior-surface-rules.json

REQ-007.conclusion: The requirement groups three sharing stories but gives no semantic partition among them. SHARE-002 and SHARE-003 are DISC-generated rows without requirement bindings.

enterpriseRemoteGap.conclusion: SHARE-003 remains cross-surface and cannot be promoted merely because enterprise sharing code exists. The already-locked enterprise/function surface still lacks a qualifying in-surface specification.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: session id plus remotely issued share id, secret and public URL
reviewedPartitions.outputs: one session_share row keyed by session id and removed with the session through the foreign-key lifecycle
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: database failures are fatal in ShareNext; create does not persist after a non-success remote response
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: secret-bearing share metadata persists in the local user database until explicit share/session deletion
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: one local row per shared session plus in-memory cache entries
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: No SHARE task is bound to the persistence row; native implementation would mutate the user database and persist a remote secret, which is outside the authorized no-user-DB lane without explicit ownership.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: existing snapshot data plus new typed session/message/part/diff/model records and share id/secret for storage-backed operations
reviewedPartitions.outputs: deterministically key-sorted last-write-wins snapshot data or typed NotFound/InvalidSecret errors
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: unknown share ids fail NotFound, mismatched secrets fail InvalidSecret, and storage failures propagate
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: the pure merge map is call-local; the surrounding share service writes unbounded snapshot data and secret-bearing metadata to enterprise storage
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: merge memory scales with the full snapshot and incoming batch; no target byte/item bound is specified
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The deterministic merge is mechanically portable but is private inside a broader storage/secret service. REQ-007 does not assign SHARE-001/004/005, SHARE-002 is generic, and SHARE-003 remains enterprise-remote blocked.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: legacy compaction state and ordered legacy share-event keys
reviewedPartitions.outputs: merged snapshot plus updated compaction marker when legacy events exist
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: storage read/write/list failures propagate; no task-specific retry or migration rollback contract is specified
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: persistent migration rewrites enterprise share snapshot/compaction state
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: reads and merges all legacy event batches for one share; no explicit data bound is specified
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This is migration/storage behavior, not a task-bound generic session-share contract, and implementing it would invent persistent remote compatibility semantics.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: HTTP create/sync/data/delete requests, share secret, optional support authorization, legacy or org endpoint selection
reviewedPartitions.outputs: share metadata, snapshot data, deletion response or authorization/validation/domain failure
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: create/delete require success responses in ShareNext; sync only logs HTTP status >=400; support admin has separate timing-safe bearer authorization
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: remote share/service state plus local auth/account/config selection and persisted local share metadata
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: external network requests, credentials and support secret; remote deployment/storage lifetime is outside the native process
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: Network, credentials, support-admin authority and hosted service lifetime are not authorized by a generic SHARE story. SHARE-003 additionally remains blocked by the enterprise-remote missing-spec record.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: location-filtered session/message/part/diff/deletion EventV2 events and current share metadata
reviewedPartitions.outputs: latest-value-per-data-key queue followed by a delayed remote sync; queue/cache are cleared on scoped finalization
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: subscriber/flush causes are logged and swallowed; failed flush removes the queued batch before transport and no retry/requeue contract is present
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: one InstanceState per location with queue/shared maps and a child scope; finalizer closes the scope and clears both maps
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: one-second delayed forks and keyed maps with no explicit global item, session or byte cap
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The upstream queue is coalescing but not explicitly bounded and its failure/retry semantics can lose a failed batch. Native subscriber/network work requires an explicit task owner and target bound/backpressure contract.

candidateFragments.inputs: multiple lists of typed share records
candidateFragments.outputs: key-sorted last-write-wins list keyed by session/message/part/session_diff/model identity
candidateFragments.failureSemantics: pure total transform for schema-valid records
candidateFragments.resourceLifetime: O(unique record keys) retained during one call; no upstream target size cap
disqualifiers: The helper is private inside the enterprise storage service and has no task-specific SHARE binding.
REQ-007 maps SHARE-001/004/005 together and does not distinguish merge ownership.
SHARE-002 is generic and SHARE-003 remains cross-surface/missing-spec blocked, so residual arithmetic cannot choose an owner.

candidateFragments.inputs: event-derived share records keyed by session and record identity
candidateFragments.outputs: latest pending value per key followed by delayed flush
candidateFragments.failureSemantics: flush/subscriber failures are logged; queued entries are removed before transport and are not requeued by the reviewed source
candidateFragments.resourceLifetime: coalescing maps and delayed fibers; no explicit item/byte/session cap
disqualifiers: No exact SHARE task owns event subscription or queue behavior.
No bounded queue/backpressure/slow-client contract exists in the pinned source/spec evidence.
The actual flush path requires HTTP transport, credentials/secret-bearing metadata and user-DB state.

historyReview.limitation: The pinned OpenCode checkout is used for the current share contracts only; unavailable historical intent is not used to assign SHARE-001..005.

closureCriteria: Each SHARE ownership decision requires explicit task-specific source, caller, direct test and genuine sharing specification evidence; REQ-007 membership, source-path order and residual intersections are not ownership proof.

SHARE-003 cannot close until its enterprise-remote missing-spec/decomposition state is resolved or deliberately replaced by narrower source-grounded ownership without weakening the existing negative evidence.

Any native queue/subscriber contract must define item/byte/session bounds, backpressure or coalescing policy, retry/loss behavior, scope/finalizer lifetime and slow/failing transport semantics before implementation.

Any persistence/network implementation must explicitly own secret lifetime, user-DB mutation, external credentials/auth, deletion guarantees and remote resource lifetime; otherwise those partitions remain blocked.
